reasons: Each rule has a matching test with a clear failure message.
Phrase and text checks are a known limit and can be bypassed by rewording.

terms.meaning: a low, base and high value for a figure, instead of one number
full-time equivalent, one person working full time
a shared capability, such as a document reader, that several processes can rely on
the agreed shape of data, such as which fields it must contain
a prerequisite that must be in place before work can start

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: File setup and imports
sections.what: Imports the estimator and its output types, shared schema types, and the test fixtures. Also imports an enabler type under a different name, marked as unused for the linter.
sections.why: Reason not stated beyond the file docstring. The unused import is marked as intentional.
sections.watch_out: The unused import is deliberate, so it is not an error.

sections.name: anyio_backend
sections.title: Async test engine selection
sections.what: Selects asyncio as the engine that runs the async tests in this file.
sections.why: Likely reason: async tests need a runner.

sections.name: current_state
sections.title: Sample current state
sections.what: Builds a sample process with one statement-spreading step taking about two hours.
sections.why: Reason not stated beyond use as shared test input.

sections.name: future_state
sections.title: Sample future state
sections.what: Builds a sample redesign: an agent that extracts figures, a moderate posture, and a document intelligence pattern by default. The pattern can be removed so tests can check the no-enabler case.
sections.why: Likely reason: the pattern is optional so tests can cover processes with no shared enabler.
sections.watch_out: Passing no pattern removes the shared enabler the tests rely on.

sections.name: payload
sections.title: Estimation payload builder
sections.what: Packages the brief, current state and future state into the input the estimator takes.
sections.why: Reason not stated beyond use as shared test input.

sections.name: output
sections.title: Fake estimator answer builder
sections.what: Builds a stand-in estimator answer with ranges for effort, shares, gains, error rate and ramp time, one declared shared enabler, one data product dependency, and a rationale. Tests can vary the shares and rationale.
sections.why: Likely reason: stands in for the model so tests run without a real call.
sections.watch_out: Share values near the top of range are used to trigger a rejection test, so changing them changes which test fails.

sections.name: TestHappyPath
sections.title: Happy path checks
sections.what: Checks the estimator returns value parameters with the expected effort base, routes to the defensible tier, passes declared shared enablers through, and offers the full enabler list in the task.
sections.why: The docstring says the finance team pushes back hardest here, which is why a stronger model is used.

sections.name: TestNoTotalsAndNoMoney (part 1)
sections.title: No totals or money fields
sections.what: Checks the output has no total, savings, cost, currency or value field, and every estimated parameter is a range. A smuggled total is rejected at construction. Rationale text narrating arithmetic, payback or net benefit is refused, and a plain rationale passes.
sections.why: Reason stated in the file docstring: the estimator emits ranges and cannot total or price.
sections.watch_out: The rationale refusal uses phrase matching, so reworded arithmetic may pass.

sections.name: TestNoTotalsAndNoMoney: test_the_module_performs_no_arithmetic_on_parameters
sections.title: Assembly has no arithmetic
sections.what: Checks the source of the assembly step contains no multiply, add, sum or divide operators. Also checks the task text says the model is not computing anything and that computing is the wrong stage.
sections.why: The comment says the assembler passes ranges through untouched.
sections.watch_out: A text search can be fooled, for example by moving arithmetic into a helper.

sections.name: TestBoundsAreEnforced
sections.title: Bounds and citations enforced
sections.what: Checks shares above one at the top of range are rejected. An over-covered estimate is retried once and accepted if valid. An enabler outside the list cannot be built. A fabricated citation is rejected with the id named. Empty evidence still produces parameters.
sections.why: The docstring says a process with no support stays in the portfolio, with wider bands applied later.
sections.watch_out: Only one retry happens, so a second bad answer fails the run.

sections.name: TestEnablerCrossCheck
sections.title: Committed enablers must be declared
sections.what: Checks an enabler the design commits to must be declared, or the estimate is rejected and retried once. An empty declared list is fine when nothing is committed. The committed enablers and the future state are shown to the estimator.
sections.why: The docstring says an undeclared enabler would never be counted for deduplication.
sections.watch_out: Declaring nothing while committing to an enabler is refused.

summary: A set of tests that checks the value estimator returns ranges for effort and benefit parameters, and cannot total, price or narrate arithmetic.
purpose: Proves the estimator supplies inputs only. Totals and money are left to code elsewhere.
why: The file docstring says the estimator emits ranges and cannot total, price, or narrate a sum. The tests check that rule at the schema, text and assembly levels.
how: Pytest loads the file. Sample current and future state are built and passed to the estimator through a fake model. Tests check the output shape, that every parameter is a range, that banned fields and arithmetic wording are refused, that shares stay within one, and that declared enablers match committed ones.
inputs: A fake model client returning scripted parameter answers, sample current state, sample future state, the process brief, and a run context.
outputs: Pass or fail results for each test. Nothing is written to disk.
risks: Phrase and text checks are limited filters. The arithmetic check is a text search, so a helper function could hide arithmetic from it.
debug: If an arithmetic check fails, check the rationale wording the fake model returned. If an enabler check fails, compare the declared enabler list with the committed enablers in the future state. If a share check fails, look at the range values in the fake answer.
